text: Agile is a way of working that helps teams build products step by step. Instead of doing all the work at once, the team works in short periods called sprints. Each sprint usually lasts two to four weeks, and at the end, the team has a working piece of the product. Every morning, they have a quick meeting called a standup, where each person shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any problems they face. The team keeps a list of tasks called a backlog, and they choose items from it for each sprint. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe what a user needs from the product. This iterative process lets the team get feedback early, make changes, and improve continuously.
